meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: The color blue.

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is in the luggage closet.
I have two blue teacups.

meanings.note: Warm greeting used alone (أهلا!), with فيك/فيكي ('welcome to you!'), or paired as أهلا وسهلا! ('you are most welcome!').

examples.trans: Hello, I am Tariq!
Welcome to Jasmine House!

meanings.note: Used constantly in the polite phrase عن إذنك ('excuse me / with your permission').

examples.trans: Excuse me, may I pass?
He asked permission before heading out.

meanings.note: Carries the direct object pronoun after بدي ('want'): هاد اللي بدي إياه ('that is what I want').

examples.trans: That is exactly what I want.
I gave it to you this morning.

meanings.note: Everyday noun for a person's or place's name; takes possessive endings directly (اسمي my name, اسمك your name).

examples.trans: What is your kind name?
My name is written here in the notebook.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: باصات.

examples.trans: The bus station is close to here.
The bus trip was comfortable.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'want / need', inflected with pronoun suffixes: بدي (I want), بدك (you want), بده (he/it wants), بدها (she/it wants), بدنا (we want), بدكم (you pl. want), بدهم (they want).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Jam bread needs unsalted butter.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

تفضّل.gloss: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are

meanings.en: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are
meanings.note: Essential Jordanian hospitality verb used mostly in the imperative: تفضل (to a man), تفضلي (to a woman), تفضلوا (plural).

examples.trans: Please have a seat, ma'am!
Here you go, hot mint tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تقيلة, plural: تقال).

examples.trans: This suitcase is very heavy today.
Take off your heavy coat and sit down to rest.

meanings.note: The standard Levantine Arabic word for 'inside' or 'inwards'.

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: Active participle of حط ('to put, place').

examples.trans: Mazen has put old boxes on the stairs.
What have you packed inside this suitcase?

meanings.note: Used warmly across ages in Jordan: يا حبيبي (to a boy/man, or as 'my goodness!') and يا حبيبتي (to a girl/woman).

examples.trans: Good morning, my dear.
A warm welcome to dear friends.

meanings.note: Standard word for a stone or rock, singular form.

examples.trans: Old stone holds warmth.
She stepped onto the stone step outside.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حجوزات.

examples.trans: I have a booking for a double room.
I read the booking ledger in the morning.

meanings.note: Core word in صباح الخير ('good morning'), مساء الخير ('good evening'), تصبح على خير ('good night'), and rising-tone خير؟ ('is everything okay?').

examples.trans: Good morning, neighbours!

examples.text: خير إن شاء الله، شو صار؟
examples.trans: Hopefully all is well, what happened?

meanings.note: Unvocalised درج covers both daraj ('stairs', masculine collective) and durj ('desk drawer').

examples.trans: Go up the stairs to the second floor.
The big notebook is inside the drawer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دفاتر.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in the booking ledger.
I forgot my leather notebook on the table.

meanings.note: Future tense marker in Jordanian and Levantine Arabic, equivalent to 'sa-' in MSA.

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: رحلات.

examples.trans: How was the bus trip today?
We wish you a happy, comfortable journey.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a number, digit, or phone number.

examples.trans: Here is your key, room number four.
Is there a phone number written on the paper?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Numeral 'seven' (عالسبعة 'at seven o'clock').

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
I booked room seven yesterday.

meanings.note: Core word in مع السلامة! ('goodbye!', literally 'with safety') and الحمد لله عالسلامة ('glad you arrived safely').

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Thank goodness for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: Paired with أهلا in the classic welcome أهلا وسهلا! ('may you find family and smooth ground — welcome!').

examples.trans: Welcome! Please come into the courtyard.
A hundred welcomes to you all!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شبابيك.

examples.trans: The window overlooks the courtyard tree.
We painted the wooden shutters in summer.

meanings.note: Singulative شجرة ('a tree', feminine), collective شجر ('trees').

examples.trans: We placed the table under the old tree.
We hear the rustle of tree leaves in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Standard everyday 'thank you' across the Arabic-speaking world.

examples.trans: Thank you all very much!
Thank you for your patience, sir.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word (from Turkish çanta) for any handbag, backpack, or travel suitcase.

examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.
We set the suitcases beside the reception desk.

meanings.note: Standard word for morning in both Classical and colloquial Arabic.

examples.trans: Good morning! How did you sleep today?
The weather is very pleasant this morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: طوابق.

examples.trans: Your room is on the second floor on the right.
The building has three storeys.

meanings.note: Form II طلّع means both 'look!' (طلّع بالمراية) and 'bring/carry up' (رح أطلّع الشنتة).

examples.text: طلع بالمراية ورا المكتب يا معلم!
examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the desk, boss!
I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.

meanings.note: The standalone number ten.

examples.trans: You arrived ten minutes early.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: A very common preposition used to indicate location, possession, or presence.

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فساتين.

examples.trans: She folded the dresses and packed them in the suitcase.
The blue dress is neat and comfortable.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.
We prepared a warm breakfast for the guests.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فناجين.

examples.trans: I set two teacups on the tray.
This is my favourite coffee cup.

meanings.note: Used as a preposition or adverb meaning 'above', 'over', or 'upstairs'.

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.
The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أقواس.

examples.text: ادخل عالساحة من هاد القوس الحجري.
examples.trans: Step into the courtyard through this stone arch.

examples.text: الأقواس القديمة مبنية من حجر عمان.
examples.trans: The old arches are built of Amman limestone.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person masculine singular. Widely used as an auxiliary verb.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: Placed AFTER the adjective or verb it intensifies: تقيلة كتير ('very heavy'), شكرا كتير ('thank you very much').

examples.trans: The smell is so good!
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: The main interrogative word for asking about manner or state.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?
Tell me how to find the shop.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ل- before nouns ('for/to'); before pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian it takes the stem إل-: إلي ('for me / mine'), إلك ('for you / yours'), إله ('his'), إلها ('hers'), إلنا ('ours'), إلكم ('yours pl.').

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is mine.
Thank you all very much!

meanings.note: Also used in the mild Jordanian exclamation يا لطيف! ('goodness gracious!').

examples.trans: Hot bread makes people pleasant!
Goodness gracious, the suitcase is so heavy!

meanings.note: Polite everyday Jordanian address for an adult woman or female guest.

examples.trans: Good morning, madam, please come in!
The room is booked under Madam Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مريحة, plural: مريحين).

examples.trans: It has a very comfortable wooden bed.
The bus ride was comfortable and calm.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Means both a door key and a mechanic's spanner/wrench (مفتاح حديد iron wrench).

examples.trans: Here is the key to room four.
We have eight brass keys on the board.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مفضلة, plural: مفضلين).

examples.trans: This is my favourite cup for tea.

examples.text: كيكة الليمون هي الحلو المفضل عندهم.
examples.trans: Lemon cake is their favourite dessert.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أماكن.

examples.trans: This place is very quiet and comfortable.
Everything is tidy in its proper place.

meanings.note: Very common word of approval or rating something highly.

examples.trans: The reading light beside the desk is excellent.
The shower water was hot and excellent!

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: We found an old music book in the suitcase.
Gentle music is soothing in the evening.

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Clear, polite 'yes' (slightly warmer and more formal than casual آه).

examples.trans: Yes, room four is on the second floor!
Yes, a hundred times yes!

meanings.note: Appears in صباح النور ('morning of light', the standard reply to صباح الخير) and نور الشمس ('sunlight').

examples.trans: Good morning and welcome!
We read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Masculine هادي ('quiet') is homographic with the feminine demonstrative هادي ('this'); context and agreement distinguish them cleanly.

examples.trans: The spot above the tree is very quiet.
We prepared the quiet attic room for you.

meanings.note: Used in negative constructions or as a strong negative emphasis.

examples.trans: Is the window facing the street or the courtyard?
Not a single drop of water on the table!

meanings.note: The standard interrogative adverb for location in the dialect.

examples.trans: Where is the computer, Tariq?
Where should I put the small spoons?

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
